Front: What is Anthropic's model hierarchy from most to least capable (June 2026)?
Back: Mythos 5 (restricted, 93.9% SWE-bench) > Fable 5 (GA premium, multi-day autonomous) > Opus 4.8 (GA high-end, adaptive thinking) > Sonnet 4.6 (GA workhorse, hybrid reasoning) > Haiku 4.5 (GA fast, 4-5x faster than Sonnet 4.5).

Front: What is the key innovation of Mythos 5?
Back: Autonomous zero-day vulnerability discovery - finds vulnerabilities in every major OS/browser without human steering, including a 27-year-old OpenBSD bug. Scores 93.9% SWE-bench Verified, 94.6% GPQA Diamond. Restricted access through Project Glasswing only (~150 organizations).

Front: What is Project Glasswing?
Back: Consortium for AI-powered defensive cybersecurity. Partners: AWS, Apple, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Google, JPMorgan, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Palo Alto Networks. ~150 organizations in 15+ countries. >10,000 high/critical vulnerabilities found. First restricted-access model tier from a frontier lab.

Front: What is "adaptive thinking" and how does it differ from "extended thinking"?
Back: Extended thinking: explicit CoT with user-set budget, tokens visible to user. Adaptive thinking: auto-adjusts reasoning depth per query, always on (no manual configuration). Adaptive replaces manual budget-setting in newest models (Opus 4.8, Fable 5, Mythos 5).

Front: What is Fable 5's key capability that distinguishes it from Opus?
Back: Multi-day autonomous work sessions. Plans across stages, delegates sub-agents, self-validates. Described as "senior research scientist grade." Same base model as Mythos 5 but safety-routed for general availability.

Front: What is Opus 4.8's key innovation?
Back: Adaptive thinking + code rigor. Auto-adjusts reasoning depth without user configuration. 4x fewer code flaws missed compared to previous versions. 61% cheaper than Opus 4.7. Best for complex reasoning + daily coding tasks.

Front: What is Sonnet 4.6's positioning in the model lineup?
Back: Hybrid reasoning (both extended AND adaptive thinking), 70% more token-efficient than predecessors, strong prompt injection resistance, near-Opus quality at 60% cost. The workhorse model for production workloads and real-time applications. 1M context.

Front: What is Haiku 4.5's value proposition?
Back: 4-5x faster than Sonnet 4.5, matches Sonnet 4 quality at 1/3 cost. Best for high-volume sub-agents and latency-critical applications. Still achieves 73.3% SWE-bench. Cheapest per-token option ($1/$5 per MTok, $0.50/$2.50 batch).

Front: What are the context window and output limits across Anthropic models?
Back: Mythos/Fable 5: 1M input, 128K output. Opus 4.8: 1M input, 128K output. Sonnet 4.6: 1M input, 64K output. Haiku 4.5: 200K input, 64K output. All support vision.

Front: What is the pricing structure for Anthropic models (per MTok output, June 2026)?
Back: Fable 5: $50. Opus 4.8: $25. Sonnet 4.6: $15. Haiku 4.5: $5 (batch: $2.50). Relative: Fable=10x Haiku, Opus=5x Haiku, Sonnet=3x Haiku. Haiku batch is cheapest at $0.50 input / $2.50 output.

Front: What is the cost-efficiency metric ($/SWE-bench %/MTok output) across models?
Back: Haiku 4.5: $0.068 (best efficiency). Sonnet 4.6: $0.187. Opus 4.8: $0.301. Fable 5: $0.556 (highest absolute quality). Haiku offers best quality-per-dollar for tasks within its capability range.

Front: When should you choose Fable 5 over Opus 4.8?
Back: Fable 5 for: multi-day autonomous projects requiring sustained planning, research tasks needing self-validation across stages, and tasks requiring sub-agent delegation over extended periods. Opus for: daily complex reasoning/coding within single sessions.

Front: What is the significance of Mythos being the first restricted-access model from a frontier lab?
Back: Demonstrates capability withholding for safety - the model autonomously discovers zero-day vulnerabilities, so broad access poses risks. Deployed only through vetted partners in Project Glasswing. Sets precedent for tiered access based on capability danger level.

Front: What benchmark scores define Mythos 5's frontier performance?
Back: SWE-bench Verified: 93.9%. GPQA Diamond: 94.6%. Humanity's Last Exam (tools): 64.7%. CyberGym: 83.1%. Terminal-Bench 2.0: 82.0%. SWE-bench Pro: 77.8%. OSWorld-Verified: 79.6%. BrowseComp: 86.9%.

Front: What Fable 5 partner benchmark achievements are notable?
Back: SOTA on: CursorBench, FrontierBench, Finance (Hebbia), Analytics (Hex - first >90%), AutomationBench (Zapier), ViBench (Replit). Demonstrates broad real-world task mastery beyond academic benchmarks.

Front: What is the tokenizer difference in newer Anthropic models?
Back: Mythos/Fable 5 use a new tokenizer that produces 30-35% more tokens than the standard tokenizer used by Sonnet 4.6 and Haiku 4.5. This affects cost calculations - same text costs more tokens with new tokenizer.

Front: What is Opus 4.8's tool use overhead?
Back: 290 tokens overhead per tool use call. This is lower than standard overhead in other models. Important for agentic workloads with many tool calls where overhead accumulates significantly.

Front: Which Anthropic models support extended thinking vs adaptive thinking?
Back: Extended thinking only: Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.5. Adaptive thinking: Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Fable 5, Mythos 5. Sonnet 4.6 uniquely supports BOTH modes.

Front: What is the decision framework for choosing Anthropic model by scenario?
Back: Multi-day autonomous: Fable 5. Security research: Mythos 5. Complex reasoning/daily coding: Opus 4.8. Production/real-time: Sonnet 4.6. High-volume/sub-agents: Haiku 4.5. Cost-optimized batch: Haiku 4.5 batch. Maximum capability: Mythos 5.

Front: What is the knowledge cutoff for each Anthropic model tier?
Back: Opus 4.8: January 2026. Sonnet 4.6: August 2025. Haiku 4.5: February 2025. Mythos/Fable 5: not stated. More capable models tend to have more recent knowledge cutoffs.

Front: What is Sonnet 4.6's advantage in prompt injection resistance?
Back: Strong prompt injection resistance is specifically called out as an innovation for Sonnet 4.6. This makes it particularly suited for production workloads where untrusted user inputs are processed and security against adversarial prompts is critical.

Front: How does Sonnet 4.6 achieve "near-Opus at 60% cost"?
Back: Hybrid reasoning (combining extended and adaptive thinking) + 70% more token-efficient generation. Produces fewer tokens for equivalent quality output. Positioned as the optimal price-performance choice for most production workloads.

Front: What makes Haiku 4.5 suitable for sub-agent workloads?
Back: 4-5x faster than Sonnet 4.5 (low latency critical for many tool calls), matches Sonnet 4 quality (capable enough for focused sub-tasks), 1/3 cost of Sonnet. Optimal for multi-agent architectures where coordinator uses Opus/Sonnet and workers use Haiku.

Front: What is Sonnet 4.6's ARC-AGI-2 score and what does it indicate?
Back: 60.4% on ARC-AGI-2 (high effort). This benchmark tests abstract reasoning and pattern recognition - the kind of novel problem-solving that requires genuine reasoning rather than pattern matching from training data. Indicates strong general reasoning capability.

Front: How does Opus 4.8 compare to Opus 4.7 in cost?
Back: Opus 4.8 is 61% cheaper than Opus 4.7 while maintaining or improving quality (especially code rigor - 4x fewer code flaws missed). Demonstrates Anthropic's trend of improving price-performance across model generations.

Front: What is the significance of Fable 5 being "same base model" as Mythos 5?
Back: Fable 5 has the same underlying model as Mythos 5 but with safety routing that prevents autonomous vulnerability discovery. This means Fable has equivalent raw capability but directed toward safe, productive autonomous work rather than security research.

Front: What vision capabilities do Anthropic models support?
Back: All current models support vision. Opus 4.8 specifically documented at 3.75MP (megapixel) resolution. Vision enables multimodal workflows: reading screenshots, analyzing diagrams, understanding UI elements.

Front: What is the batch pricing advantage for Haiku 4.5?
Back: Haiku 4.5 batch: $0.50/MTok input, $2.50/MTok output (50% discount vs real-time). Best option for high-volume asynchronous processing where latency is not critical. Most cost-effective option in the entire Anthropic lineup.

Front: What does the >10,000 vulnerabilities found by Mythos mean for AI safety discourse?
Back: Demonstrates dual-use nature of frontier AI: same capability that finds defensive security vulnerabilities could be misused offensively. Anthropic's response (restricted access via consortium) is a novel governance model - capability exists but deployment is controlled.

Front: How should you route between Sonnet and Haiku in a production system?
Back: Use Haiku for: simple classification, extraction, formatting, sub-agent tasks, high-throughput pipelines. Use Sonnet for: complex reasoning, nuanced generation, tasks requiring extended context understanding, customer-facing responses requiring high quality. Route based on task complexity.

Front: What is the key trend represented by "adaptive thinking replaces extended thinking"?
Back: Moving from manual configuration (user sets thinking budget) to automatic scaling (model decides how much to think). Reduces user burden of parameter tuning. Newest models auto-adjust reasoning depth per query - easy questions get fast answers, hard questions get deep thinking.

Front: What SWE-bench scores across the Anthropic lineup show the capability gap?
Back: Mythos 5: 93.9%. Opus 4.8: ~83%. Sonnet 4.6: 80.2%. Haiku 4.5: 73.3%. The 20+ point gap between Mythos and Haiku represents substantial capability difference, but Haiku still resolves 3/4 of real GitHub issues.

Front: What is the "Opus 4.8 Fast" variant and its pricing?
Back: Opus 4.8 Fast: $10 input / $50 output per MTok (2x standard Opus price). Trades cost for lower latency. Same model quality but optimized serving for latency-sensitive applications. Same pricing tier as Fable 5.

Front: How many organizations have access to Mythos 5 and what restricts broader access?
Back: ~150 organizations in 15+ countries through Project Glasswing consortium. Restricted because Mythos autonomously discovers zero-day vulnerabilities in production systems. Safety concern: broad access could enable offensive security use.

Front: What is the practical implication of Opus 4.8's "self-correction" capability?
Back: Opus 4.8 can detect and correct its own errors during generation - noticing logical inconsistencies, code bugs, or reasoning flaws and fixing them in-line. This reduces the need for external verification loops and improves single-pass output quality.

Front: How does the 30-35% tokenizer inflation in newer models affect cost comparisons?
Back: Same text produces 30-35% more tokens with Mythos/Fable's new tokenizer. At $10/$50 per MTok, this means effective cost is ~30% higher than raw token pricing suggests when comparing to models using the standard tokenizer. Must account for this in cost analysis.

Front: What makes Fable 5 "senior research scientist grade"?
Back: Capability to: plan across multi-day stages, delegate sub-tasks to other agents, self-validate intermediate results, sustain coherent work across extended sessions, and produce research-quality output autonomously. Represents shift from tool to autonomous collaborator.

Front: What is the maximum output length difference between model tiers?
Back: Mythos/Fable/Opus: 128K tokens max output. Sonnet/Haiku: 64K tokens max output. The 2x difference matters for tasks requiring very long generated responses (comprehensive code generation, detailed reports, long-form analysis).

Front: Why might Haiku 4.5 be preferred over Sonnet for certain tasks despite lower benchmarks?
Back: Haiku is 4-5x faster with 1/3 cost. For tasks where quality difference is minimal (extraction, classification, simple edits), the speed and cost advantages dominate. Also better for latency-sensitive user-facing applications where sub-second response matters more than marginal quality.

Front: What is the significance of the 27-year-old OpenBSD bug found by Mythos?
Back: Demonstrates that AI can find vulnerabilities that decades of human security research missed. The bug existed since ~1999 in one of the most security-focused operating systems. Validates the transformative potential of AI-powered security auditing.
